content:
Urban II’s description of Jerusalem as “the navel of the world,” a place made holy by Christ’s life and death, and currently held by “unclean nations,” is intended to inspire Christians to reclaim it.  
This fits into the broader call for a Crusade, which was framed partly as an armed pilgrimage to free a holy site central to Christian faith.  
The emphasis on pilgrimage to Jerusalem was a major theme in the speech, even though the military aspect is prominent — the underlying religious context is the importance of Jerusalem as a pilgrimage destination now inaccessible or under non-Christian control.  

Final answer: (A)
